Sum the distinct multiples, below a limit, of any of a list of factors.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/sum-of-multiples) (MIT). Listed under [Numbers & Math](/examples/?subject=numbers-and-math).

```nomi-run
// FILE: sum_of_multiples.nomi
/// The sum of every number below `limit` that is a multiple of at least one
/// of `factors`. Each multiple counts once, and a factor of 0 has none.
pub fn sum(factors: List<Int>, limit: Int) -> Int {
    factors
    |> Iter.filter(&(&1 > 0))
    |> Iter.flat_map(fn factor -> Range.step_by(factor..limit, factor))
    |> Iter.to_set()
    |> Iter.sum()
}

// FILE: sum_of_multiples_test.nomi
import sum_of_multiples

test "sums the multiples" {
    cases = [
        #("no multiples within limit", [3, 5], 1, 0),
        #("one factor has multiples within limit", [3, 5], 4, 3),
        #("more than one multiple within limit", [3], 7, 9),
        #("more than one factor with multiples within limit", [3, 5], 10, 23),
        #("each multiple is only counted once", [3, 5], 100, 2318),
        #("a much larger limit", [3, 5], 1000, 233168),
        #("three factors", [7, 13, 17], 20, 51),
        #("factors not relatively prime", [4, 6], 15, 30),
        #("some pairs of factors relatively prime and some not", [5, 6, 8], 150, 4419),
        #("one factor is a multiple of another", [5, 25], 51, 275),
        #("much larger factors", [43, 47], 10000, 2203160),
        #("all numbers are multiples of 1", [1], 100, 4950),
        #("no factors means an empty sum", [], 10000, 0),
        #("the only multiple of 0 is 0", [0], 1, 0),
        #("the factor 0 does not affect the sum of multiples of other factors", [3, 0], 4, 3),
        #(
            "solutions using include-exclude must extend to cardinality greater than 3",
            [2, 3, 5, 7, 11],
            10000,
            39614537,
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, factors, limit, expected), description {
        assert sum_of_multiples.sum(factors, limit) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The solution follows the instructions' wording: the multiples of each factor (`Range.step_by(factor..limit, factor)`), combined into a `Set` to drop duplicates, then summed with `Iter.sum`. Filtering `1..limit` by "divisible by any factor" was the other natural form; the set form says what the problem says.
- A factor of 0 is filtered out before stepping, since it has no positive multiples and `step_by` by 0 would not end. The filter is `Iter.filter(&(&1 > 0))`, one comparison, so the capture reads more directly than `fn factor -> factor > 0`; the `flat_map` after it uses the factor twice and stays a lambda.
- One `subtests` table for all 16 cases.
